question: Do persisted compacted replacement-history records account for most of the bytes in one observed multi-gigabyte Codex session store?

sources.name: OpenAI Codex source
sources.claim: Current public source serializes a full replacement_history into each compacted rollout item and reconstructs from persisted compacted checkpoints.

sources.name: OpenAI Codex configuration reference
sources.claim: history.max_bytes and history.persistence govern history.jsonl; the reference documents no equivalent rollout-session byte cap.

sources.name: Existing public oversized-rollout report
sources.claim: The public issue already owns the oversized-rollout hydration and app-server memory consequence.

sources.name: Existing public replacement-history report
sources.claim: The public issue already owns repeated compacted replacement-history growth in subagent rollouts.

environment.platform: macOS 26.6.1 (25G76), arm64; ChatGPT Desktop 26.818.61809 build 7019; codex-cli 0.149.0-alpha.4.3

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Compacted records are a minority of retained bytes.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Tool outputs or another record class, rather than checkpoint persistence, dominates this incident.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Compacted records are the majority of retained bytes and dominate the largest rollouts.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Repeated full replacement-history checkpoints are the primary on-disk amplification mechanism in this incident.

stop_condition: Stop after a content-safe scan attributes retained bytes by rollout record class and current public source identifies the persistence boundary.
